question: For the FINAL Effluent Limits table entries showing "Report MGD" (Flow), "Report" (Total Dissolved Solids), and "Report" (Daphnia pulex WET NOEC), does the permit impose an enforceable numeric effluent limit for compliance comparison, or only a monitoring and reporting obligation without a numeric limit against which reported values may be evaluated for exceedance?
source_locator: farmington/final_permit.pdf page 4 section part_i (Flow; Total Dissolved Solids, Discharge (*6) and Water Plants Intake (*7)); farmington/final_permit.pdf page 5 section part_i (Daphnia pulex WET NOEC)
semantic_arguments: "Report" and "Report MGD" appear in the MINIMUM/MAXIMUM limit columns (30-DAY AVG, DAILY MAX, 7-DAY AVG), not solely in MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY or SAMPLE TYPE columns

Other pollutants in the same table carry explicit numeric limits (e.g., BOD5 30 mg/L, E. Coli 126 cfu/100 mL) or minimum thresholds (e.g., BOD5 Percent Removal > 85), contrasting with "Report" entries
Flow maximum columns show "***" alongside "Report MGD" in the average columns, which may indicate absence of a numeric maximum limit

Footnotes *6 and *7 define reporting methodology (geometric mean of weekly values) for TDS Discharge and Water Plants Intake rows without stating numeric effluent limits in those rows; numeric limits for TDS Net Increase appear on separate rows with footnotes *10 and *11

Footnote *9 cross-references PART II for additional WET monitoring and reporting conditions not included in this passage, leaving uncertain whether numeric WET pass/fail criteria apply to Daphnia pulex

Purpose A requires distinguishing enforceable numeric limits from report-only monitoring; Purpose B and Purpose C require determining monitoring applicability and the semantics of results without ordinary numeric reported values
notes: Bounded semantic obligation covering all three highlighted target spans. Resolution would determine whether reported measurements for these parameters undergo numeric exceedance comparison (Purpose A), how monitoring requirements are classified (Purpose B), and how missing or non-numeric results are interpreted (Purpose C). Does not resolve whether "Report" denotes report-only obligations or assert any factual compliance outcome.
